records.rationale: The overheating hazard is real, but undersized fusing is not an accurate general explanation for failure to interrupt a hard MOV short: a lower current rating ordinarily clears earlier, while inadequate interrupting capacity is a different issue. MOV thermal runaway can occur below a conventional fuse's clearing threshold. Silent-until-smoke and the blanket unprotected-is-safer comparison are also unsupported.

evidence.title: Littelfuse integrated overcurrent/overtemperature protection
evidence.finding: MOVs can overheat under abnormal sustained voltage even with upstream fusing; coordinated thermal protection may be required.

Current-rating coordination, interrupting rating and thermal-disconnect behavior are separate protection properties; the adjective undersized cannot substitute for identifying which one is inadequate.
